text: A trained model is a frozen snapshot of patterns learned at one point in time, but the real world it serves keeps moving. Customer behavior shifts, fraud evolves specifically to evade whatever's deployed, markets change overnight — none of that requires a single line of the model's code to change for its accuracy to quietly decay. Ninety-four percent at deployment is a claim about one moment, not a permanent guarantee, and that's exactly the gap monitoring exists to catch.

Data drift is a shift in the statistical distribution of input features in production compared to training data — detectable with tests like the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test or the Population Stability Index, comparing live traffic against the training baseline feature by feature. The useful part is that this doesn't require waiting for anything else to happen; it's visible the moment incoming data starts to look statistically different.
That's the early-warning half of the picture — a p-value crossing a threshold flags that a feature's distribution has moved, well before anyone confirms whether predictions are actually wrong yet.

Model drift is the more direct concern: an actual, measurable drop in predictive performance compared to deployment time. The catch is that measuring it needs ground-truth labels — did the prediction turn out to be right — and those often arrive on a real delay, a confirmed fraud case might take days. That's exactly why data drift tends to be the earlier signal: it doesn't have to wait on labels at all.

None of this matters if an alert just sits in a dashboard nobody opens. The entire design, matching lesson nineteen's pipeline, is that a drift alert fires the retraining trigger directly — the same repository dispatch event from that pipeline definition. Monitoring detects the problem, CI/CD retrains and re-evaluates automatically, and the gate decides if the result actually deserves to replace what's live.

That closes the full circuit: data preparation, training, evaluation, deployment, and monitoring from lesson seventeen, made reproducible by the tracking and registry from lesson eighteen, automated end to end by the CI/CD pipeline from lesson nineteen, and kept honest in production by the drift detection you just learned. That's the complete MLOps pipeline for model lifecycle management.
